{
  "decision": "approve" | "reject" | "escalate",
  "confidence": <number 0-1>,
  "reasons": [
    { "dimension": "<e.g. completeness, consistency, contract>", "finding": "<what you found>",
      "evidence_ref": "<optional pointer>" }
  ],
  "blocking_questions": ["<string>", ...],
  "advisory": [
    { "kind": "ac_quantifiability", "ac_id": "<optional AC id>", "finding": "<what is semantically unmeasurable>" }
  ]
}
RULES:
- decision "escalate" REQUIRES at least one entry in blocking_questions.
- Every OTHER decision REQUIRES blocking_questions to be an EMPTY array.
- Prefer "escalate" over guessing when evidence is genuinely ambiguous or missing —
  a wrong confident answer is worse than an honest escalation.
- If ANY pre-check above has outcome "fail", you should almost always decision="reject"
  or "escalate", not "approve".
- reasons MUST have at least one entry.
- OPTIONAL "advisory": zero or more non-blocking AC-quantifiability findings; omit the key or use [] when none. advisory findings are ADVISORY ONLY. They MUST NOT by themselves cause you to set decision="reject" — the deterministic lint is the sole hard gate. Use them to inform a reviewer, not to block.
- DESIGN NECESSITY (dimension "design_necessity", applies to every document type): decide whether the document introduces ANY of (a) a stopgap or temporary seam, (b) a bespoke guard check, scanner or ledger whose purpose is to guard a design constraint, (c) a silent fallback that substitutes a value for a missing required input, (d) a phased or transitional migration with intermediate states. For each one found, ask whether an end-state design would make it unnecessary. If yes, you MUST return decision "reject" with a reasons entry whose dimension is "design_necessity", naming each such item and the end-state alternative. A check, fallback or phase that the end-state design itself requires (for example a behavioural acceptance test of the design, or a user-visible degraded mode the document defines) is not a finding when the document says why it is necessary.
